_baseline.note: T3 baseline established by reading Risk Factors + Legal Proceedings/Contingencies of the four relevant 10-Ks. Same-family AI/content-risk language is present in every year, but no ADI incident event is named. Only one incident (997, Kadrey copyright litigation) is specifically disclosed via named litigation in Meta's own periodic reports.

quotes: objectionable content made available on our products by third parties
use of our products or services for illicit or objectionable ends
we also may fail to respond expeditiously or appropriately to the sharing of objectionable content
susceptible to algorithm or other technical errors
reductions of advertising by marketers due to objectionable content made available on our products by third parties
use of our products or services for illicit or objectionable ends, including ... geopolitical events, or elections
develop new product features using generative AI ... may result in new or enhanced governmental or regulatory scrutiny, litigation, ethical concerns, or other complications
risks related to harmful or illegal content, accuracy, misinformation (including related to elections), bias, discrimination, toxicity
cannot guarantee that third parties will not use such AI technologies for improper purposes, including through the dissemination of illegal, inaccurate, defamatory or harmful content
provision of our services to younger users; FTC administrative proceeding alleging COPPA violations
harmful or illegal content, accuracy, misinformation and deepfakes (including related to elections), bias, discrimination, toxicity
inaccurate, defamatory or harmful content, intellectual property infringement or misappropriation
third parties using Meta's open-source Llama models could engage in intellectual property infringement or misappropriation
exposure to litigation over training data and model outputs; child safety / COPPA administrative proceeding

997.evidence: efts q='Kadrey' &ciks=1326801 = 13 hits in Meta's OWN periodic filings, first appearing in FY2023 10-K (0001326801-24-000012, meta-20231231.htm, filed 2024-02-02) and multiple subsequent 10-Qs (e.g. 0001326801-24-000049 Q1-2024). Kadrey et al. v. Meta Platforms is the copyright class action alleging Meta used copyrighted/pirated books (incl. via LibGen shadow library) to train its Llama LLMs - the exact subject of this incident. (efts q='LibGen' = ZERO HITS; the matter is disclosed under the case name Kadrey.) FY2023/FY2024 10-K Risk Factors independently flag AI 'intellectual property infringement or misappropriation' and training-data litigation exposure.
997.accounting_channel: Loss contingency / legal proceedings disclosure (Commitments & Contingencies note; IP-litigation reserve channel). Litigation narrative is not XBRL-tagged so verbatim text could not be extracted from R-files; presence confirmed via full-text search of the primary 10-K/10-Q documents.
specific_queries: "Kadrey" (13 hits across Meta 10-K/10-Q/ARS - company disclosure)
"LibGen" (ZERO HITS)
997.rationale: The specific incident (using copyrighted/pirated books to train Llama) is disclosed via the named Kadrey copyright litigation in Meta's own periodic reports; the matter is inherently AI-training-data framed. Coded T1 (disclosed-specific). Confidence medium because verbatim AI-framing sentence could not be extracted from the truncating full document, though the named Kadrey matter is unambiguously the AI-training-copyright case.
